title: Rework dashboard query paths to scale usage analytics (cursor pagination, indexes, caching)
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Several Console dashboard endpoints that surface customer usage and activity (per-token cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, model usage leaderboards) are showing tail latencies and high DB CPU on peak. The endpoints rely on ad-hoc pagination, multiple large JOINs against raw telemetry, and no consistent caching strategy. This causes slow dashboard loads, increased infra cost, and intermittent 5xxs under heavy queries from customers and internal analytics jobs.

Goal: Reduce p95 latency for dashboard query APIs by 50% on average for common queries and bring backend DB CPU for analytics routes down by at least 30% during peak. Provide stable pagination behaviour (cursor-based) and introduce targeted materialized/pre-aggregated paths and caching to serve common query shapes without sacrificing freshness beyond SLA requirements.

Approach summary: 1) Replace offset-based pagination with opaque cursor tokens (last-seen-timestamp + shard id) for large result sets to avoid expensive OFFSET scans. 2) Add covering and partial indexes catering to high-cardinality filters (customer_id + route + day). 3) Create incremental materialized tables for 1h and 24h rollups for cost/usage aggregates with realtime upsert pipeline. 4) Introduce a lightweight route-level Redis cache for short-lived aggregation results with cache keys tied to query fingerprint + dataset_version. 5) Denormalize small, frequently-joined entities into analytics tables to eliminate late-stage JOINs. 6) Add query planner hints and use prepared statements for stable plans. 7) Implement streaming chunk responses for large result sets using continuation cursors and backpressure friendly server-side streaming.

Why different from previous ticket: Prior work (ENG-4827) focused on dashboard query indexing and adaptive pagination. This ticket targets high-cardinality analytics workloads, explicit materialized rollups, cache invalidation semantics tied to dataset versions, and the migration path to cursor-based streaming for very large leaderboards and exports.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for analytics dashboard APIs reduced >= 50% for representative queries in staging
DB CPU consumption for analytics routes reduced >= 30% in synthetic peak tests
Offset pagination removed from identified endpoints; cursor-based pagination implemented with backward-compatible client tokens
Cache layer added and instrumented with hit/miss metrics; baseline hit rate >= 40% for 1h rollup queries
Materialized 1h and 24h rollup tables exist with automated incremental refresh pipeline and documented TTL
End-to-end integration tests for pagination cursors, cache invalidation, and rollup correctness added to CI
Migration plan and rollback instructions documented in Confluence and reviewed by SRE
tasks: Spike: benchmark current queries and capture p50/p95/p99, query plans, and hot indexes (owner: Evan)
Design: define cursor token format and client compatibility layer (owner: Maya)
DB: add partial and covering indexes for top-10 slow filters (owner: Priya)
Data pipeline: implement incremental upserts for 1h/24h rollups using existing analytics ETL (owner: Tomas)
Cache: implement Redis route-level cache with dataset_version aware keys and TTL defaults (owner: Leila)
API: replace offset params with cursor parameter, support legacy offset for 4 weeks via middleware (owner: Evan)
Backend: add streaming chunked responses and backpressure handling for exports (owner: Carlos)
QA: synthetic peak test harness and load test scenarios for analytics endpoints (owner: QA Team)
Telemetry: add dashboards for cache hit rate, cursor error rate, p95 latency, DB query time per endpoint (owner: Observability)
Rollout: canary enable behind feature flag; monitor and auto-rollback rule if error rate >1% or p95 increases (owner: SRE)
Docs: Confluence runbook for cache invalidation, migration steps and rollback instructions (owner: Maya)
Security: review for any new authorization surface for cached query responses (owner: Security)
PRs: link code changes and DB migrations in the ticket (owner: each implementer)
Postmortem: collect learnings after rollout in #infra-postmortems channel (owner: Evan)
comments: 2026-02-22 - Spike results: initial profiling shows three queries responsible for 70% of analytics CPU on staging. OFFSET-based leaderboards are the worst offenders with linear scan time on larger pages.
2026-02-25 - Decision: use opaque base64 cursor composed of (last_event_ts, partition_id, dataset_version). Will include a server-side validation layer to allow skipping for legacy clients.

2026-02-28 - DB patch: Priya applied partial index on (customer_id, day) WHERE event_type = 'token' in staging; p95 for the query dropped ~38% but write amplification observed on heavy ingestion windows.
2026-03-03 - Data pipeline: Tomas validated incremental upsert prototype. 1h rollup generation latency ~20s for 1M events; plan to batch commits and use upsert sharding to reduce concurrency.

2026-03-06 - Cache prototype: Leila implemented route cache with 60s TTL; initial hit rate ~46% for dashboard queries during typical traffic. Edge case: near-real-time freshness customers will bypass cache via cache_bypass flag.
2026-03-08 - API PR: Evan opened PR #5146 for cursor parameter and streaming response; awaiting code review from Carlos and Leila. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5146
2026-03-09 - Load test: Synthetic peak with 4x baseline QPS shows DB CPU down 33% vs baseline and p95 improved 52% for targeted endpoints in blue environment.
2026-03-10 - Blocker: one downstream job depends on offset semantics for exported CSVs. Adding a migration shim to translate cursor to offset for exports; estimated 2d work.
